summary: Use Button when one clear action moves someone forward, confirms a choice, or completes a task.

placementAdvice.text: Place the action where the decision happens, and let surrounding content explain the choice.

from.quote: Use surrounding content to explain the choice. Let the button stay concise.

placementAdvice.text: In a wide container, keep the action close to the content it completes.

from.quote: Keep the action close to the content it completes.

placementAdvice.text: Make one action the strongest; competing actions should not share equal emphasis.

from.quote: Two dominant actions make the choice harder to read.

placementAdvice.text: Let container width resolve the layout: the same action can fill a narrow container's width. There is no separate desktop or mobile Button.

from.quote: Container width resolves the layout. Designers choose the label, hierarchy, and size—not a separate “desktop” or “mobile” Button.

configuration.text: Use type default for most actions; it hugs its label or fills its container when the layout asks it to.

from.quote: The standard solid action. It hugs its label or fills its container when the layout asks it to.

configuration.text: Use type fixed for aligned, bounded actions: it keeps long content within the system width limit.

from.quote: Keeps long content within the system width limit. It remains responsive rather than using a hand-set pixel width.

configuration.text: Do not use type fixed for a full-width action: fixed is bounded by the system and will not fill. Use type default for a footer action that fills its container.

from.quote: Fixed is bounded by the system and will not behave like Fill.

configuration.text: Use type glass only over a meaningful backdrop such as rich media or a coloured surface.

configuration.text: Do not place type glass on a plain, low-contrast surface: it loses its purpose and can become hard to read.

rules.text: Make the action clear before choosing its appearance; the label should explain what happens next.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text to display when no children are provided. Default "Button", from the component source.

props.name: children
props.description: Optional custom content to render inside the button. When provided, this is treated as a full-content override and `label`/`labelStyle` are ignored.

props.name: renderContent
props.description: Optional render prop for taking over the inner label/content while still reusing the token-driven text styles. When provided, this takes precedence over `children`. The `styles` argument is the merged text style (base token styles + `labelStyle`). Example: ```tsx <Button renderContent={(styles) => ( <CustomText style={styles}>Pay now</CustomText> )} /> ```.

props.name: leading
props.description: Optional leading accessory (e.g., icon)

props.name: trailing
props.description: Optional trailing accessory (e.g., icon)

props.name: icon
props.description: Name of the icon to display on the right side of the button. Takes precedence over `trailing` if both are provided.

props.name: type
props.description: Visual/layout type matching the Figma `Type` property. Defaults to `'default'`. `'glass'` also activates when `modes['Button type'] === 'glass'`. Default "default", from the component source.

props.name: glassOverlayColor
props.description: Glass-only override for the translucent overlay color painted over the live blur. Defaults to the resolved `button/background` token under `Button type=glass`. Ignored for non-glass types.

props.name: glassIntensity
props.description: Glass-only override for blur intensity on the 0–100 scale. Defaults to the `blur/minimal` token. Ignored for non-glass types.

props.name: modes
props.description: Mode configuration passed to the token resolver (e.g., {"Button / Size": "M"})

props.name: onPress
props.description: Callback triggered when the button is pressed.

props.name: disabled
props.description: When true, the button cannot be pressed. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: style
props.description: Optional style overrides for the button container.

props.name: labelStyle
props.description: Optional style overrides for the label text.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessibility label for screen readers. If not provided, uses label or children text.

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: Additional accessibility hint for screen readers.

props.name: accessibilityState
props.description: Additional accessibility state information Performance notes: - The pressed visual (background/border swap) is applied through the Pressable `style` callback, NOT a mirrored React state. This avoids the flicker that scrolling parents previously caused: when a ScrollView cancels a touch the host view simply reverts its style without React rendering. On iOS we additionally use `unstable_pressDelay` so the pressed visual is never even applied during a scroll-cancelled touch. - Hover state is only mirrored into React state on web (where hover events fire). On native the setter call is gated out so the component never re-renders due to hover. - All design-token reads are folded into a single `useMemo` keyed on `(modes, disabled)`. - The component is wrapped in `React.memo`. Callers that want to take advantage of this should pass stable `modes` (the default `EMPTY_MODES` is already stable) and stable callback props. /.

props.name: webAccessibilityProps
props.description: Web-specific accessibility props (only used on web platform)

props.name: loading
props.description: Explicit per-instance loading override. When `true`, the button renders as a pill-shaped skeleton of the same size; when `false`, the surrounding `<SkeletonGroup>` is ignored. Defaults to inheriting from the group.

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: When `true`, disables text truncation: the trailing ellipsis (`…`) is never shown and any `numberOfLines` clamp is ignored, so the text wraps to as many lines as it needs even when horizontal space is tight.

props.name: ...SafePressableProps
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.
